_comment: The catalogue the app fetches to discover installable stem models.
This copy is the source of truth kept in the repository. The published
copy is uploaded as a release asset and is what the app actually reads;
tools/publish-model.py rewrites the url, sha256 and sizeBytes fields from
a real archive so those three are never typed by hand.
The models array is empty because nothing has been converted and hosted
yet. An empty catalogue is a valid document: the app parses it, finds
nothing to offer, and falls back to the built-in DSP separator, which
needs no model at all.
Fields, and which of them matter:
id               stable across versions; identifies the model, not the build
version          semver. Compared numerically per component, so 1.10.0
sorts above 1.9.0
format           ONNX or QNN
backend          CPU or QNN. QNN assets are per-SoC, see htpArchs
url              https only. The app refuses plain HTTP because the
archive is verified against a hash from this same
document, and fetching both over HTTP would let one
attacker rewrite both
sha256           64 hex characters, checked before the model is installed
sizeBytes        checked against the downloaded length before hashing
license          metadata, shown in the model details
sourceModel      what it was converted from, for the model card
stems            which stems this model actually produces. Omit and it
means the classic four; a six-stem model has to say so
modelSampleRate  the rate the weights expect
segmentFrames    the window the model was trained on. Getting this wrong
does not fail loudly, it just separates badly
minimumAndroid   API level
abi              arm64-v8a
htpArchs         QNN only. Context binaries are compiled per Hexagon
architecture, which is why one universal NPU asset is
not a thing. See MODEL_CARD.md, Appendix A
